title: The Weight of Memory
tagline: the fifth boss - cleanup you cannot forget
hints: `#include <memory>` for unique_ptr and make_unique, `#include <utility>` for std::move.
`horde.push_back(std::make_unique<Goblin>());` - make_unique builds it and hands the vector sole ownership. There is no `new` anywhere on this floor.

Loop with `for (const auto& m : horde)` when reading and `for (auto& m : horde)` when changing. A plain `auto m` would try to COPY a unique_ptr, which is forbidden on purpose - copying it would mean two owners.
`survivors.push_back(std::move(m));` hands ownership over. Afterwards `m` is empty - that is the point, there is only ever one owner.
`m.reset();` destroys what a unique_ptr holds, right now. On a pointer whose contents were already moved away it does nothing at all - which is exactly why the survivors do not dissolve in that loop.
Torch is pure RAII: a constructor that prints, a destructor that prints, nothing else. Declare it FIRST in main so it is destroyed LAST.
